comments.body:
Premise CONFIRMED in code: `explain_material_change` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/material_diff.py) emitted CHECKBOX_NOTE on only the 'no material component differs' branch and the degraded pre-component-hashing branch; the primary `delta is not None` early return — the branch a CURRENT attestation takes — returned the named delta with no note.

Fix pushed as Gerrit change 1637 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1637), message-text only:
- AC1: the named-delta branch now appends the same CHECKBOX_NOTE.
- AC2: a diagnostic, non-basis `description_boxes` component (checkbox-state hash + ticked count) rides alongside the existing `material-part:` lines, so when `description` changed the message says 'its TEXT changed, checkbox state is unchanged' or 'its TEXT changed, and checkbox state changed too (0 -> 2 ticked), which is NOT the cause'. It is absent from COMPONENT_ORDER, so the composite fingerprint and describe_delta ignore it — no gate outcome can change. Pre-diagnostic attestations get no clause rather than a guess.
- AC3: held-out tests in tests/unit/plan_review/test_94a3_material_diff.py cover tick-only (no staleness), AC-text edit (stale + note + 'checkbox state is unchanged'), text+ticks (both separated), and the degraded no-clause path.

Local gates: 189 plan_review tests pass, make lint and make typecheck clean, module 407 LOC (cap 800).

compiled_state.description:
# The stale-material message omits the checkbox note on its PRIMARY path

`material_diff.CHECKBOX_NOTE` is introduced with this comment:

    #: The advice every material-staleness reason carries, because it is the single most
    #: frequently mis-believed fact about the gate (bug 94a3, observations 1 and 3).

It is not carried by every reason. `explain_material_change` emits it on only TWO branches:

  * material_diff.py:301 — the "no material component differs" branch (an attestation that
    predates AC-checkbox normalization);
  * material_diff.py:323 — the degraded branch (an attestation that predates component-level
    fingerprinting).

The PRIMARY branch — `delta = describe_delta(signed, current); if delta is not None: return
delta` (material_diff.py:295-297) — returns the named delta with NO note. That is the branch
a current attestation takes, so it is the one almost every author actually sees.

## Observed
Closing task b2bb after ticking its ACs *and* appending evidence prose to each AC item
produced, verbatim:

    plan-review close gate: stale-material: the plan was materially edited since review —
    changed: description (8208 -> 8829 chars). Health: current (no related material)
    (enforced); phase planning -> execution (compatible)
    Run rebar review-plan b2bb-fa81-e054-4fb5 separately, then retry close.

No checkbox note. The author had just been REQUIRED by the close precheck to tick boxes, so
the tick is the salient recent edit and the natural (wrong) conclusion is that ticking staled
the review. That is exactly the misconception bug 94a3 recorded three agents making; this one
made a fourth, with the preventing sentence present in the codebase but not on this path.

## This is a MESSAGE defect, not a gate defect
The gate is correct and its behaviour should not change:
  * ticking `- [ ]` -> `- [x]` is normalized out of the fingerprint and is attestation-SAFE;
  * editing the TEXT of an acceptance criterion IS a change to the plan and SHOULD require a
    fresh review. That is the point of binding the material.
Only the explanation is deficient, and only on the branch that matters most.

## Secondary: the delta names the component but not what moved inside it
`changed: description (8208 -> 8829 chars)` identifies WHICH basis key changed, not what
within it. An author who ticked boxes AND edited prose in one `rebar edit` cannot tell from
the message which of the two is responsible — the char delta is consistent with both.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The named-delta branch of `explain_material_change` carries `CHECKBOX_NOTE` too, so
      every `stale-material` reason states that a tick is never the cause. (The module
      comment already claims this is true; make it true.)
- [ ] When the changed component is `description`, the message distinguishes "checkbox state
      changed as well" from "item text changed" — enough for the author to know which edit
      staled the attestation, without printing the diff.
- [ ] Held-out test: a description edit that ONLY flips checkbox state yields no staleness; an
      edit that changes AC item text yields `stale-material` AND a reason containing the
      checkbox note.

## NOT part of this ticket — the documentation is adequate
An earlier draft of this bug claimed the docs fail to tell an author to record AC evidence in
a COMMENT rather than in the AC text. That claim was withdrawn on review: the guidance is
already present and sufficient.
  * `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md:209` shows evidence recorded as a ticket
    comment;
  * `:304` states that comments are non-material and do not stale an attestation;
  * the completion verifier's own failure text instructs the author to "add a comment to this
    ticket that documents the concrete artifacts".
Annotating AC text with evidence instead is an author error, not a doc gap, and editing that
text SHOULD stale the review because it changes the plan. Nothing here asks for a doc change.

## Provenance
Hit while closing b2bb during the store/signing remediation. Cross-references bug 94a3
(the three prior agents) and bug 330c (the normalization that makes ticking safe).

## Implementation plan
All changes in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/material_diff.py` (+ manifest feed), message text
only — no gate outcome changes.

1. **AC1 — note on the primary branch.** In `explain_material_change`, the
   `delta is not None` early return gains the same `CHECKBOX_NOTE` tail the other two
   branches already carry, so every `stale-material` reason states that a tick is never the
   cause.
2. **AC2 — say what moved inside `description`.** Box state is normalized out of the signed
   component hash, so the signed side carries no box information today. Add a DIAGNOSTIC
   (non-basis) component `description_boxes` = (hash of the checkbox-state sequence, number
   ticked), emitted alongside the existing `material-part:` lines. It is NOT a basis key: it
   is absent from `COMPONENT_ORDER`, so `describe_delta` ignores it, the composite
   fingerprint is untouched, and `material_components` keeps returning exactly the basis
   keys (asserted by `tests/unit/plan_review/test_94a3_material_diff.py:81`). A new helper
   feeds `reviewed_material_parts` / `_current_components` the basis PLUS the diagnostic.
3. When `description` is among the changed components, the message appends whether the
   checkbox state also changed (with a ticked count delta) or is unchanged; when the
   attestation predates the diagnostic line, the clause is omitted (graceful degradation,
   same posture as the existing degraded branch). No ticket content is ever printed.

## Verification
- `tests/unit/plan_review/test_94a3_material_diff.py` gains held-out cases:
  a description edit that ONLY flips box state produces NO staleness (composite unchanged);
  an edit to AC item text produces a delta whose reason contains `CHECKBOX_NOTE` and the
  text-vs-box discrimination; an old (pre-diagnostic) manifest still explains without it.
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `pytest tests/unit/plan_review/` all green.

## File impact
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/material_diff.py`
- `tests/unit/plan_review/test_94a3_material_diff.py`
